defaults.permitted_development: Across East Sussex, detached domestic garages are usually easiest on the planning permission route when they stay clearly secondary to the house, respect height and boundary relationships, and avoid creating a more dominant frontage or access arrangement. Visible frontages and more open plots can make roof form, materials and street impact more sensitive than a simple garage sketch suggests.

rules.height_rules: Garage proposals across East Sussex are normally judged first on overall height, eaves height and whether the roof form keeps the building subordinate to the main house.
rules.depth_rules: Across East Sussex, garage depth and footprint are usually most straightforward when the building sits in a logical side or rear position and leaves enough garden and turning space around it. Very deep or bulky garages can stop feeling incidental even if the height looks modest.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary siting, neighbour relationship and vehicle access are the recurring pressure points for garages in East Sussex, especially where a new crossover or tight turning arrangement is involved.
rules.roof_rules: Low-profile garage roofs are generally easier than taller roof forms that create storage volume, apparent accommodation or a more dominant outbuilding shape.
rules.materials_rules: Garages are normally easiest to support when the materials, door treatment and overall appearance sit comfortably with the house and local street scene.

rules.permitted_development: In Eastbourne, a detached garage is usually easiest to keep off the formal planning permission route when it remains clearly secondary to the house, sits comfortably within the plot and does not create a more dominant frontage or access arrangement. The answer usually gets harder when the garage is pushed forward in the plot and starts to compete with the house on the street frontage.

rules.height_rules: In Eastbourne, garage height is usually the first measurement to sense-check, especially where the building sits close to a boundary or uses a taller pitched roof.
rules.depth_rules: A garage in Eastbourne is more likely to need a closer review if the footprint starts to dominate the garden or front part of the site rather than sitting as a modest supporting structure.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary siting, neighbour impact and highway practicality all matter in Eastbourne, particularly if the garage depends on a new or altered vehicle access.
rules.roof_rules: Garage roofs in Eastbourne are usually easiest where they stay low-profile and do not suggest loft storage, accommodation or a second-storey form.
rules.materials_rules: Materials and frontage treatment should help the garage read as a subordinate domestic building in Eastbourne, not as a visually dominant addition to the property.

restrictions.conservation_area: Garages in conservation areas within Eastbourne often receive a closer design review where they affect the character of a visible frontage or the wider street scene.
restrictions.listed_building: Garages affecting a listed building or its setting in Eastbourne usually need a more careful planning and heritage consent check.
